Former Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai is charged with dangerous driving and other offences and is out on bail awaiting trial. He served as a legislator from December 2022 to July this year. According to a review of LegCo records by The Collective, Wong's office operation expenses over his more than 42-month term exceeded HK$10 million, including over HK$1.5 million in consultancy fees. He successively appointed Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association" which he himself founded, and vice-president Ng Hok-ling, as consultants. Chan Tak-ming had been continuously engaged since January 2023, receiving HK$20,000 to HK$30,000 per month, totalling over HK$1 million in consultancy fees. According to the LegCo guidelines on applications for reimbursement of operating expenses, "a Member should not employ as a consultant his political party or any company/organisation in which his political party has a controlling interest." Is there a problem with hiring officials of a related organisation as paid consultants? The Legislative Council Secretariat replied to The Collective's enquiry, stating that the guidelines have already set out the provisions and that no further comment would be made. Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliation, responded that the association's work is voluntary and that it operates on a non-profit basis. In addition, towards the end of his first term, Wong also distributed bonuses to his office staff, and that month he declared over HK$773,000 in staff expenses to LegCo.

Office operating expenses during term exceeded HK$10 million

The Collective reviewed Wong Kam-fai's "reimbursement amounts for office operating expenses" in the Seventh Legislative Council, which ranged from about HK$2.877 million to HK$2.984 million annually; from October 2025 onwards, in the Eighth Legislative Council, the amount has been raised to HK$3.02 million. During his 42 months in office, Wong declared office operating expenses exceeding HK$10 million to LegCo. In 2023 and 2024, his declared expenses were approximately HK$1.876 million and HK$2.89 million respectively.

However, in 2025, Wong's declared expenses amounted to HK$4.006 million. The increase in expenses was attributable to, among other things, staff expenses rising from HK$2.24 million the previous year to HK$3.215 million; consultancy fees also rising from HK$480,000 to HK$640,000. After Wong was re-elected in 2026, his expenses from January to June amounted to HK$1.413 million.

Spent over HK$1 million to hire senior executives of his own association as legislative consultants

According to records, from February 2023 to June 2026, Wong Kam-fai declared consultancy fees exceeding HK$1.5 million to LegCo. During the 36 months from 2023 to 2025, he consistently engaged Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association," at HK$30,000 per month, spending HK$1.08 million. After Wong was re-elected to the current term until his resignation, within six months, he continued to engage Chan Tak-ming at HK$20,000 per month, spending a total of HK$120,000. The "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association" was founded by Wong Kam-fai in 2016, and he serves as its executive president.

Three consultancy tenders, two bidders were members of the "Association"

As early as March 2023, Wong Kam-fai submitted tender documents to LegCo for declaration. At the time, the three consultancy tenders were from Tai Ching-fung, Chan Tak-ming, and Cheng Kwok-wai. Both Tai and Chan are members of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association," with Tai serving as head of the finance group. Tai quoted HK$45,000, Cheng quoted HK$35,000, and Chan quoted the lowest price of HK$30,000; ultimately Chan was awarded the consultancy work.

The tender scope of work stated that Chan's consultancy duties included assisting in advocacy and planning for innovation and technology, education, various social policies and issues; facilitating interaction and communication across different sectors; and assisting in supporting various regional office operations.

Hired association vice-president as consultant with only one bid

Wong Kam-fai also engaged association vice-president Ng Hok-ling as a consultant. From June 2023, Ng Hok-ling served as Wong's consultant on innovation and technology and education policy matters, receiving a consultancy fee of HK$5,000 in the first month, and subsequently HK$10,000 per month, totalling HK$315,000. For Ng Hok-ling's consultancy work, there was only one bid. Regarding the scope of work in the tender, Wong stated that Ng "is concurrently familiar with both innovation and technology and education policies," "can respond quickly to work requirements with flexible service arrangements, and the service quality meets the needs of his parliamentary work."

LegCo guidelines: Should not employ organisations controlled by political parties as consultants

According to Article 24 of the LegCo "Guidelines on Applications for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses by Members," "a Member should not employ as a consultant his political party or any company/organisation in which his political party has a financial interest or controlling interest." Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliation: The association operates on a non-profit basis

The Collective enquired with Wong Kam-fai whether engaging officials of a related organisation as consultants might conflict with the guidelines. Wong replied that Chan Tak-ming's role was regional and political liaison, while Ng Hok-ling was in the education sector. Wong stated that the association was founded by a group of like-minded innovation and technology professionals hoping to contribute to innovation and technology development in Hong Kong and the Mainland, "Everyone serves on a voluntary basis, and it has always operated on a non-profit basis." According to records, Wong Kam-fai has no political affiliation.

Office director received HK$276,000 in salary upon contract completion

Aside from consultancy expenses, regarding the remuneration expenses of legislative assistants, according to records, when Wong Kam-fai completed his term in 2025, he declared two staff expense items totalling over HK$773,000 to LegCo, of which approximately HK$423,000 was for paid leave, together with November and December salaries.

Wong also distributed approximately HK$350,000 in bonuses to five office staff. Among them, Wong's office director had a monthly salary of HK$63,500. Upon completion of her term in December, she received paid annual leave compensation, together with two months' salary totalling approximately HK$181,000, plus a bonus equivalent to 1.5 months' salary of HK$95,200, totalling HK$276,000. The other four staff members received bonuses from Wong equivalent to 2.5 months' salary, ranging from HK$54,000 to HK$75,000.

Legislative Council Secretariat: Guidelines for reimbursement of operating expenses have been set out

The Collective previously enquired with the Legislative Council Secretariat as to whether it was appropriate for Wong Kam-fai to engage the president and vice-president of his own association as long-term consultants, and to distribute bonuses. The Secretariat replied that the relevant details have been set out in the LegCo guidelines on applications for reimbursement of operating expenses by Members, and no further comment would be made.

"LegCo Members' Guidelines on Applications for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses" Guiding Principles (partial) ・Members or their relatives should not have any direct or indirect financial interest in transactions involving applications for reimbursement. ・Members should avoid applying for reimbursement for any transaction that would lead the public to believe that they, their relatives, or business partners could benefit therefrom. ・Members should adhere to the principles of openness, fairness and accountability when using public funds. ・Where conflicts of interest cannot be avoided or have already arisen, Members should declare their interests when applying for reimbursement, and the declarations will be available for public inspection. ・If a transaction for which reimbursement is or may be applied for gives rise to a suspicion of conflict of interest on the part of a Member, the Member should handle such matters in accordance with the principle of public interest. ・Members should, as far as possible, keep their private affairs/interests separate from those of the Legislative Council, and should make the public aware that they are doing so in the performance of their duties, so as to avoid any suspicion of conflict of interest or improper private gain.

LegCo Members' Guidelines on the Use of Consultancy Services: Members may engage consultants on a permanent or ad hoc basis... To avoid conflicts of interest, the following requirements must be met: ・Individual contracts should be signed with each engaged consultant ・Contracts should clearly specify the scope of services provided by the consultant ・The name of the consultant and the fees charged should be listed on the reimbursement application documents for public inspection ・A copy of the contract should be submitted to the Secretariat (the contract need not be available for public inspection) ・Members or their relatives should not have any interest relationship with the engaged consultants ・Members should not employ as a consultant their political party or any company/organisation in which their political party has a financial interest or controlling interest

In the declaration records, Wong Kam-fai labelled the bonus amount as "other," stating that no bonuses had been disbursed in the three years prior to his term and that this was a discretionary arrangement, "hence it was not specified in the contract." He also stated that the team had jointly promoted and implemented various bills, motions and initiatives, and that "after prudent consideration of the office's financial position, a decision has been made to disburse bonuses to the following staff members in recognition of their hard work and contributions during the Seventh Legislative Council term." According to the "Guidelines on Applications for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses," Members may set aside funds from the reimbursement amount for office operating expenses to pay for staff contractual bonuses, double pay, or end-of-contract gratuities. The amount set aside should be determined based on contracts signed by both parties and other legal obligations, and should not be excessive; Members may receive disbursements without the need to submit supporting documents.

On 29 June this year, Wong Kam-fai was arrested by police on four charges including suspected drink driving and careless driving after allegedly hitting two vehicles within the CUHK campus and fleeing the scene. Wong was exposed by the media on 1 July for failing to declare his involvement in the case to LegCo, and had previously attended the Handover anniversary reception as usual for photo-taking, until 3 July, when Wong resigned from all his duties at the Legislative Council.

Aside from being a LegCo member from the Election Committee constituency, Wong Kam-fai is also a member of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and Associate Dean (External Affairs) of the CUHK Faculty of Engineering. Following the drink driving incident, CUHK announced the suspension of his administrative duties to date. In September this year, police formally charged him with four offences including "dangerous driving," and he was granted bail, with the case adjourned to 11 November for further mention.
